meta.title: The Book That Wore Out
meta.skill_frame: Use facts in the passage to work out something it does not say directly.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is three links: handling causes wear, one copy was borrowed far more, and demand is why a second copy helps. Measured FK 5.1-6.9 on the 3 parts (Flesch-Kincaid, approximate syllable count). The load sits inside the grade 4-5 band and rises across the stage.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for inference 4.3, sequence 4. No external work.
source.survey: Written to the stage: everyday subject, stated facts, links held apart.
source.avoided: No named real places or people. No figures that could go stale.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance and number of links, climbing one knob per sequence.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A library bought two copies of the same book on the same day. One copy sits in the children's room and the other in the adult section. After a year the children's copy is falling apart, and the adult copy looks new. Both are the same printing and the same binding.
passage.part_2: The children's copy was borrowed 74 times. The adult copy was borrowed 9 times. A book wears out from handling, not from age. Each loan means the cover is opened, the spine is bent, and the pages are turned. Children also tend to read in shorter sittings, so a borrowed book goes back and forth more often.
passage.part_3: The librarian did not change suppliers. She replaced the children's copy with a reinforced binding and bought a second copy for that room.

tutor_only.correct_reason: The fourth sentence says the children's copy is falling apart and the adult copy looks new.
tutor_only.tell: The children's copy is falling apart. The adult copy still looks new.
help: Find the sentence about the two copies after a year.
accept_ideas: the one in the children's room

if_they_say.ask: One looks new. Which one is falling apart?

items.prompt: Both copies are the same printing and binding. What does that rule out?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. It rules out a defective copy.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Identical manufacture means the difference cannot be in the book itself, so it has to be in use.
tutor_only.tell: If one were badly made it would explain the damage. They were made the same way.
help: Think about what would explain one copy failing if they were made differently.
They were not. So what is left?
tutor_only.core_idea: It rules out a badly made copy.
accept_ideas: it rules out a bad copy

if_they_say.when: the student says the children's copy was cheaper
if_they_say.ask: The passage says same printing and binding. What else could differ?

items.prompt: Why did the children's copy wear out first?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It was borrowed 74 times against 9.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage gives the two loan counts and says wear comes from handling, so more loans means more wear.
tutor_only.tell: Seventy-four loans against nine. Every loan bends the spine and turns the pages.
help: Then find the sentence about what handling does.
tutor_only.core_idea: It was borrowed far more often, and handling is what wears a book.

if_they_say.when: the student says children are rougher
if_they_say.ask: The passage names handling and loan counts, not carelessness. Which one does it measure?

items.prompt: Children read in shorter sittings. How does that add to the wear?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The book goes back and forth more often.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says shorter sittings mean more trips back and forth, and each trip is another loan.
tutor_only.tell: A book read in short pieces is borrowed, returned, and borrowed again. More trips mean more handling.
help: Find the sentence about shorter sittings.
Look at what that does to the number of loans.
tutor_only.core_idea: It means more loans, and more loans mean more handling.

if_they_say.when: the student says children damage books
if_they_say.ask: The passage is about trips, not damage. What does a short sitting increase?

items.prompt: Why did the librarian buy a second copy rather than a stronger one alone?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The demand is the cause, so more copies share the handling.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage shows wear tracking loans, and the fix is a reinforced copy plus a second copy for the same room.
tutor_only.tell: One strong copy still gets borrowed 74 times. Two copies split the handling between them.
help: Look at what caused the wear.
Then look at what splits that cause between two books.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because demand caused the wear, so a second copy shares the handling.
accept_ideas: more copies means less handling each
not_required: how long a book should last

if_they_say.when: the student says the first copy was poor quality
if_they_say.ask: The passage rules that out. What did it say about loans?

advance.next_means: The first lesson in the next inference stage.
advance.student_line: You have the move. The next reading is another lesson on this skill.

retry.student_line: The next reading is another lesson on this skill in this stage.
